leads.name: Antoniusbaum (Sankt-Vith)
leads.verify_progress: 2026-09-07 partial check: protected as landscape of the German-speaking Community of Belgium since 10-10-1985 (Wikidata Q57352818 and the English/Dutch Wikipedia lists of protected heritage sites in Sankt-Vith both confirm the designation and give a precise Wikidata coordinate, used here). Neither source gives species, age, girth or any story/folklore beyond the name (Antonius = Saint Anthony, so likely a devotional tree similar in kind to Herchies' chene a clous, but that is inference, not sourced). No news coverage or visitor-destination evidence found in the time available. Needs: species, age/girth, and evidence of why anyone would seek it out specifically (a local history source or the 'Unsere Gemeinde' municipal newsletter PDF at st.vith.be may have this, not fetched this pass). Does not currently pass the destination test on available evidence; a from-scratch pass with more time on ostbelgienkulturerbe.be (the region's own heritage database, linked from the Wikipedia entry) could change that.

leads.name: Die sieben Brüder (Solwaster)
leads.verify_progress: 2026-09-07 partial check: WebSearch found no Belgian sources at all for this name (it collided with an unrelated, much more famous German Sieben-Bruder-Eiche near Friesack, Brandenburg). The Commons photo filenames (Sawe-Jalhay, Gospinal, Solwaster) place it in the Jalhay area near Spa, and the species is almost certainly oak (Quercus robur JPG file names). No age, girth or narrative found; likely needs a French or Walloon-dialect search ('sept freres' or the Walloon name) rather than German, since Jalhay is French-speaking and 'die sieben Bruder' may be a German nickname used by German-speaking visitors rather than the local name. Not verified this pass.
